angles: Zero-trust credential injection: Agents never see secrets — tokens injected at the network layer via outbound Workers handlers
Dynamic egress policies: Lock down sandbox network access after initial setup using setOutboundHandler to switch from 'allow hosts' to 'no HTTP'
The three-layer Cloudflare security stack for agents: Outbound Workers (egress proxy) + Cloudflare Mesh (private networking) + Managed OAuth (identity-aware access)
Evolution of Outbound Workers: From Workers for Platforms (intercept customer Worker fetch requests) to Sandbox/Container outbound handlers (intercept all agent egress)
Under the hood: Ephemeral CAs, TLS MITM proxying, TPROXY nftable rules, and proxy-everything sidecar for local dev
Comparison of agent authentication methods: Standard API tokens (leaky) vs OIDC workload identities (complex) vs custom proxies (manual) vs Outbound Workers (zero trust by default)
Six-level evaluation hierarchy: Understanding the deniedHosts → allowedHosts → handler chain for building secure sandbox policies
Per-instance identity-aware policies: Use ctx.containerId to scope credentials to specific sandbox sessions via KV lookups
Always-on observability: Outbound Workers logging integrates with Workers dashboard and Logpush for egress monitoring
